questions.q: How does SQL Server resolve a deadlock?
options: It automatically picks one transaction as the 'deadlock victim' and rolls it back, raising an error for the application to handle
It permanently locks the database until an administrator intervenes
It merges both transactions into one
It ignores the deadlock and lets both transactions proceed anyway
questions.explain: The other transaction proceeds normally; the victim's application typically needs to retry.

questions.q: What is a common practical cause of deadlocks, and how can it be avoided?
options: Two transactions locking the same two tables in opposite order — avoided by accessing tables in a consistent order
Deadlocks are entirely random and cannot be reduced by any coding practice
Using too many SELECT statements in a single session
Declaring too many variables in one script
questions.explain: This is one of the practical mitigation strategies alongside keeping transactions short and designing for retry.
